title: I Want to Build a Granny Flat

eligibility.heritage_restrictions: Not available on heritage items without DA

steps.title: Check Your Eligibility
steps.description: Verify your property meets the basic requirements for a secondary dwelling (granny flat) under SEPP Housing 2021.
tasks: Obtain a Section 10.7 Planning Certificate from your council
Check your lot size meets minimum requirements (typically 450sqm)
Verify your zoning allows secondary dwellings
Confirm no heritage, flood, or bushfire overlays that restrict CDC
tips: Use the NSW Planning Portal to check basic zoning
Your 10.7 certificate will list all constraints

steps.title: Understand the Rules
steps.description: Learn the key development standards that your granny flat must comply with to use the fast-track CDC pathway.
tasks: Review SEPP Housing 2021 Division 2 requirements
Check your council's DCP for local requirements
Understand setback requirements (usually 3m rear, 0.9m side)
Note the maximum 60sqm floor area limit
tips: Private certifiers often provide free initial consultations
The 60sqm limit includes any covered outdoor areas

steps.title: Engage Professionals
steps.description: Assemble your project team including designer and certifier.
tasks: Engage a building designer or draftsperson for plans
Get quotes from 2-3 private certifiers
Consider a surveyor for accurate site measurements
Obtain a BASIX certificate (energy and water efficiency)
tips: Private certifiers are typically faster than council
Ask certifiers about their turnaround times upfront

steps.title: Prepare Documentation
steps.description: Compile all required documents and plans for your CDC application.
tasks: Prepare architectural drawings (site plan, floor plans, elevations, sections)
Obtain BASIX certificate
Commission structural engineering if required
Prepare stormwater management plan
Compile specification documents
tips: Your certifier can provide a checklist of required documents
Incomplete applications are the #1 cause of delays

steps.title: Lodge CDC Application
steps.description: Submit your Complying Development Certificate application through the NSW Planning Portal.
tasks: Create NSW Planning Portal account
Upload all documentation
Pay application fees (typically $1,500-3,000)
Respond to any requests for information promptly
tips: Lodge via the NSW Planning Portal for faster processing
Keep copies of all submitted documents

steps.title: Construction Phase
steps.description: Build your granny flat with required inspections.
tasks: Appoint a Principal Certifier (often same as your CDC certifier)
Notify council 2 days before construction starts
Complete mandatory inspections at each stage
Keep detailed records of all work
tips: Don't proceed past inspection stages without approval
Weather can significantly impact construction timelines

steps.title: Get Your Occupation Certificate
steps.description: Complete final inspection and obtain approval to occupy.
tasks: Request final inspection from Principal Certifier
Ensure all conditions of consent are met
Obtain Occupation Certificate
Notify council of completion
tips: You cannot legally occupy or rent without an OC
Keep your OC safe - you'll need it for insurance and sale

common_pitfalls: Exceeding the 60sqm floor area limit (covered areas count)
Not checking for easements or sewer lines on site
Assuming CDC is available on heritage or flood-affected land
Starting work before CDC is issued
Not meeting minimum setback requirements
Forgetting to include car parking requirements

title: I Want to Add a Second Storey

eligibility.height_limit_check: Must comply with LEP height limits
eligibility.existing_structure: Structural assessment of existing building required

steps.title: Assess Feasibility
steps.description: Determine if your property can accommodate a second storey under local planning controls.
tasks: Obtain Section 10.7 Planning Certificate
Check LEP height limits for your zone
Check Floor Space Ratio (FSR) limits
Engage structural engineer to assess existing foundations
Review any heritage or conservation area restrictions
tips: Height limits vary significantly between zones (often 8.5-9.5m in R2)
Existing FSR usage will limit how much you can add

steps.title: Choose Your Pathway
steps.description: Determine if CDC or DA is required based on your property constraints and design ambitions.
tasks: Review Codes SEPP Part 3 Division 1 for CDC eligibility
Check if you meet all CDC standards (setbacks, height, privacy)
Assess if any Clause 4.6 variations will be needed
Consult with architect or certifier on recommended pathway
tips: CDC is faster but requires strict compliance with standards
DA allows more design flexibility but takes longer

steps.title: Engage Design Professionals
steps.description: Assemble your project team for design development.
tasks: Engage an architect or building designer
Engage structural engineer for foundation assessment
Consider a town planner if DA pathway
Commission site survey if not recently done
tips: Architects can help maximize design within constraints
Get structural advice early - foundation upgrades can be costly

steps.title: Design Development
steps.description: Develop your design to comply with all relevant controls.
tasks: Develop concept design within planning constraints
Prepare shadow diagrams showing impact on neighbours
Address privacy impacts with screening or setbacks
Ensure design meets BCA requirements
Obtain BASIX certificate
tips: Shadow diagrams are critical for neighbour amenity assessment
Consider early consultation with neighbours

steps.title: Prepare and Lodge Application
steps.description: Compile documentation and submit your application.
tasks: Prepare full architectural drawing set
Prepare Statement of Environmental Effects (if DA)
Compile all specialist reports
Lodge via NSW Planning Portal
Pay application fees
tips: DA fees are based on estimated construction cost
Consider pre-lodgement meeting for complex designs

steps.title: Assessment and Approval
steps.description: Navigate the assessment process and respond to any requests.
tasks: Respond promptly to any requests for information
Address any objections through design amendments if needed
Review conditions of consent carefully
Accept any required modifications
tips: RFIs stop the assessment clock - respond quickly
Conditions may require changes to your design

steps.title: Construction and Completion
steps.description: Build your addition with required inspections.
tasks: Appoint Principal Certifier
Notify council before starting
Complete all mandatory inspections
Obtain Construction Certificate before building work
Obtain Occupation Certificate upon completion
tips: Second storey work often requires temporary accommodation
Weather can significantly impact roof removal timing

common_pitfalls: Not checking foundation capacity early enough
Exceeding height limits without realising
Underestimating neighbour privacy and shadow impacts
Not accounting for heritage area requirements
Forgetting to check FSR limits before designing
Starting work before Construction Certificate is issued

title: I Want to Build a Duplex
target_user: Investor or homeowner seeking dual occupancy

eligibility.subdivision_potential: Torrens title requires minimum lot sizes per dwelling

steps.title: Verify Dual Occupancy is Permitted
steps.description: Confirm dual occupancy development is allowed on your site under local planning controls.
tasks: Obtain Section 10.7 Planning Certificate
Check LEP land use table for your zone
Verify minimum lot size requirements are met
Identify whether attached or detached dual occupancy is allowed
Check for any site-specific restrictions
tips: Some R2 zones prohibit dual occupancy
Attached dual occ often has lower minimum lot size requirements

steps.title: Understand Development Standards
steps.description: Learn the key planning controls that will shape your duplex design.
tasks: Review height limits and Floor Space Ratio (FSR)
Check minimum setback requirements
Review landscaped area requirements
Understand car parking requirements (usually 1-2 per dwelling)
Check if the Affordable Rental Housing SEPP applies
tips: SEPP Housing 2021 may provide bonus FSR for dual occupancy
DCP controls often have minimum private open space requirements

steps.title: Plan Your Subdivision Strategy
steps.description: Decide whether to subdivide and what title type to pursue.
tasks: Decide: Torrens title, Strata title, or retain as single lot
Check minimum subdivision lot sizes in your LEP
Consult with surveyor about subdivision feasibility
Consider service connections for each lot
tips: Torrens title is more valuable but has stricter requirements
Strata subdivision can be done after construction

steps.title: Engage Professional Team
steps.description: Build your team of consultants for design and approvals.
tasks: Engage architect experienced in dual occupancy
Engage town planner for DA preparation
Commission site survey
Engage geotech if site has slope or soil issues
Consider pre-DA consultation with council
tips: Town planners can significantly improve approval chances
Pre-DA meetings help identify issues early

steps.title: Design and Documentation
steps.description: Develop your design and prepare DA documentation.
tasks: Develop dual occupancy design within controls
Prepare Statement of Environmental Effects
Complete BASIX certificates for both dwellings
Prepare shadow diagrams and privacy analysis
Address stormwater, landscaping, waste management
tips: Each dwelling needs its own BASIX certificate
Consider future residents' needs in unit mix

steps.title: Lodge and Assess DA
steps.description: Submit your Development Application and navigate assessment.
tasks: Lodge DA via NSW Planning Portal
Pay application fees (based on construction value)
Respond to Requests for Information
Address any neighbour objections
Review and accept conditions of consent
tips: Dual occupancy DAs typically take longer than single dwelling
Be prepared to negotiate design changes

steps.title: Construction and Subdivision
steps.description: Build your duplex and complete any subdivision.
tasks: Obtain Construction Certificate
Appoint Principal Certifier
Complete construction with all inspections
Apply for Occupation Certificate
Lodge subdivision application if proceeding with Torrens/Strata
tips: Subdivision can often be lodged during construction
Strata plans require registered surveyor

common_pitfalls: Not verifying dual occupancy is permitted in your zone
Underestimating minimum lot size requirements for subdivision
Ignoring solar access requirements for southern dwelling
Not planning for separate service connections
Designing without considering future subdivision requirements
Forgetting about waste collection access requirements

title: I Want to Knock Down and Rebuild
target_user: Homeowner or developer replacing existing dwelling

eligibility.heritage_restrictions: Generally not permitted on heritage items
eligibility.tree_preservation: May require arborist report for significant trees
eligibility.contamination: May need assessment if previous industrial/commercial use

steps.title: Site Assessment and Due Diligence
steps.description: Thoroughly assess your site constraints before committing to demolition.
tasks: Obtain Section 10.7 Planning Certificate
Check for heritage listing or conservation area
Identify any protected trees on site
Check for contamination history
Review all easements and services locations
tips: Heritage items typically cannot be demolished
Tree removal often needs separate approval

steps.title: Understand Site Potential
steps.description: Determine what can be built on your cleared site.
tasks: Review LEP height and FSR controls
Check minimum setback requirements
Understand landscaped area requirements
Review garage/parking requirements
Consider future subdivision potential
tips: A cleared site often enables larger builds than additions
Corner lots may have additional setback requirements

steps.title: Choose Approval Pathway
steps.description: Decide between CDC (fast-track) or DA based on your design goals.
tasks: Review Codes SEPP requirements for CDC eligibility
Assess if your design can meet all CDC standards
Consider if any variations are needed (requires DA)
Evaluate heritage/conservation area implications
tips: CDC can save months but requires strict compliance
DA gives more flexibility for unique designs

steps.title: Engage Design Team
steps.description: Assemble your professional team for design and approvals.
tasks: Engage architect or building designer
Commission detailed site survey
Engage geotechnical engineer if required
Engage arborist if significant trees present
Consider project builder for design-build approach
tips: Project home builders often include approvals in their package
Custom architects offer more design flexibility

steps.title: Design and Documentation
steps.description: Develop your new dwelling design and prepare approval documents.
tasks: Develop architectural design within controls
Prepare all required drawings and specifications
Obtain BASIX certificate
Prepare stormwater management plan
Commission structural engineering
tips: Design for your lifestyle needs, not just maximum size
Consider future-proofing (accessibility, solar orientation)

steps.title: Obtain Approvals
steps.description: Submit and obtain necessary approvals for demolition and construction.
tasks: Apply for demolition approval (often combined with construction)
Lodge CDC or DA via NSW Planning Portal
Pay application fees
Respond to any requests for information
Obtain approval before any demolition work
tips: Demolition of dwelling over 50 years may need assessment
Asbestos requires licensed removal contractor

steps.title: Demolition Phase
steps.description: Safely demolish existing structure.
tasks: Engage licensed demolition contractor
Arrange asbestos testing and removal if required
Notify council before demolition starts
Disconnect all services safely
Ensure proper waste disposal and site clearing
tips: Asbestos removal is mandatory before demolition
Some materials may be recycled or salvaged

steps.title: Construction and Completion
steps.description: Build your new dwelling with required inspections.
tasks: Obtain Construction Certificate
Appoint Principal Certifier
Complete all mandatory inspections
Obtain Occupation Certificate before moving in
Arrange final service connections
tips: Plan temporary accommodation during construction
Weather can significantly impact build timelines

common_pitfalls: Not checking heritage status before purchasing
Underestimating asbestos removal costs
Assuming larger builds are always better
Not planning for temporary accommodation
Forgetting about existing mature trees
Demolishing before approvals are in place
source_document: EP&A Act - Demolition and Building Work

title: I Want to Subdivide My Property
target_user: Property owner seeking to create separate lots

eligibility.minimum_lot_size: Varies by LEP - often 450-600sqm per lot
eligibility.access_requirements: Each lot must have legal road access

steps.title: Check Subdivision Potential
steps.description: Determine if your property can be legally subdivided under planning controls.
tasks: Obtain Section 10.7 Planning Certificate
Check LEP minimum lot size requirements
Verify minimum frontage requirements are achievable
Identify any restrictions (easements, covenants)
Check if heritage or conservation area applies
tips: Minimum lot sizes vary significantly between councils
Corner lots often have better subdivision potential

steps.title: Understand Subdivision Types
steps.description: Choose the right subdivision approach for your situation.
tasks: Evaluate Torrens title subdivision (separate land titles)
Consider Strata subdivision (shared land, separate units)
Understand Community title (mix of private and common)
Assess battle-axe lot configuration if limited frontage
Consider staged subdivision options
tips: Torrens title is most valuable but has strictest requirements
Battle-axe lots have specific access handle requirements

steps.title: Engage Professional Team
steps.description: Build your subdivision team.
tasks: Engage registered surveyor (mandatory for subdivision)
Engage town planner for DA preparation
Consult with civil engineer for services design
Check with utility providers about connection feasibility
tips: Surveyors handle the technical subdivision plan
Town planners improve approval prospects significantly

steps.title: Design the Subdivision
steps.description: Develop your subdivision layout and address technical requirements.
tasks: Prepare draft subdivision plan showing proposed lots
Design access arrangements for each lot
Plan service connections (water, sewer, electricity, NBN)
Address stormwater management
Consider building envelopes for new lots
tips: Think about what can be built on each lot
Service connection costs can be significant

steps.title: Lodge Development Application
steps.description: Submit your subdivision DA for council assessment.
tasks: Prepare Statement of Environmental Effects
Lodge DA via NSW Planning Portal
Pay application fees
Respond to Requests for Information
Address any neighbour submissions
tips: Subdivision DAs are assessed against LEP minimum lot standards
Council may require contributions for new lots

steps.title: Complete Subdivision Works
steps.description: Construct required infrastructure and satisfy conditions.
tasks: Complete any required civil works
Install service connections to each lot
Construct any required access roads
Pay developer contributions (Section 7.11/7.12)
Satisfy all conditions of consent
tips: Some conditions can be satisfied at subdivision registration
Infrastructure costs can be substantial for larger subdivisions

steps.title: Register Subdivision
steps.description: Finalize the legal subdivision and create new titles.
tasks: Surveyor prepares final subdivision plan
Obtain Section 88B instrument if needed (easements, restrictions)
Council issues Subdivision Certificate
Lodge plan at NSW Land Registry Services
Receive new Certificate(s) of Title
tips: Registration creates the new legal lots
Each new lot will have its own folio identifier

common_pitfalls: Not checking minimum lot size requirements first
Underestimating service connection costs
Ignoring frontage requirements for battle-axe lots
Not accounting for access handle width requirements
Forgetting about Section 7.11/7.12 contributions
Assuming existing dwelling can remain in any location
